properties.decision: The install registers reflow2 with the agent at USER scope — the MCP server, the ten slash commands, the coherence-loop hooks and a `reflow2` command on PATH — so every project on the machine has it with no per-project setup. `reflow2_init.py` survives, but its job narrows: it writes the pointer file and project-scope config for a repo OTHER PEOPLE work on, so their agent is told reflow2 governs this code. Solo work needs none of it. Anthony's call, 2026-07-28, choosing "machine-wide, repo init optional" over "machine-wide only" and over "keep per-project, just make it one word".
properties.name: reflow2 installs once per machine; the in-repo half is optional and only for repos you share
properties.rationale:
WHY NOT "MACHINE-WIDE ONLY", which is simpler: a teammate cloning the repo would get no signal that reflow2 governs it unless they had already installed reflow2 themselves and thought to look. That is the invisibility `req:kit-reaches-the-agent` was raised for, and retiring the per-project installer would rebuild it deliberately.

WHY NOT "JUST MAKE IT ONE WORD" (`reflow2 init .` instead of a python path): it fixes the typing and none of the arithmetic. Still one step per project, still a re-run after every upgrade, and still the case that a user who forgets it experiences reflow2 as absent.

WHAT MADE MACHINE-WIDE SAFE TO CHOOSE AT ALL, and without it the answer would have been different: the server is registered with `--only-if-present`, so a directory that never opted into a design gets the LATENT surface and nothing is created in it. Without that flag, a user-scope registration would drop a RocksDB store into every folder a session is ever opened in — and litter in someone's repo is a worse first impression than the setup step it removed. The loop-nudge hook is gated the same way and for the same reason: registered globally, silent wherever `.reflow2/` does not exist.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: `dec:skills-served` and `req:thin-install` stand exactly as they were. The skills and working instructions are still served, still never copied, and upgrading reflow2 still produces no diff in a consumer repo. This decision is about WHERE the pointers are installed, not about what is served — and it makes the thin install thinner, since the common case now installs nothing into a project at all.
